source_review.notes: Reviewed Herlihy-Wing's primary definition, Wing-Gong's primary testing/verification method, Lowe's primary testing algorithms, Horn-Kroening P-compositionality, Burckhardt et al. Line-Up, Michael-Scott queue points, and current maintainer repositories for Porcupine and OpenJDK JCStress. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Tool/project claims remain limited to their current primary repositories; passing tests are never represented as universal proof.

evidence: Checked invocation/response histories, completed and pending operations, per-process projections, completion extension, real-time order, and overlap.
Checked sequential state machine, transition relation, candidate checker state, witness, and invalid/unknown/malformed/unsupported outcomes.
Checked operation count, concurrency width, explored/memo states, checker time, unknowns, and failures remain search/empirical quantities.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation matches the finite-history definition and does not impose response order on overlapping calls.

evidence: Recomputed valid register predecessors: only W2 response at 2 precedes R2 invocation at 3; W1 overlaps both.
Recomputed DFS witness W1,W2,R2 in three explored legal candidates and final read result 2.
Recomputed invalid history: W1 must precede R0, write changes state to 1, read result 0 mismatches after two explored candidates.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Exact explored counts apply only to the model's input order and first-witness depth-first strategy, not checker complexity generally.

evidence: Verified response-before-invocation edges are mandatory while overlapping calls remain reorderable subject to the sequential specification.
Verified predecessor-ready state-machine search is sound for the model's complete deterministic finite histories and exhaustive branch exhaustion refutes the invalid fixture.
Verified formal pending-operation handling may require completing some pending calls before projecting, so unconditional dropping is unsound.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Nondeterministic specs, distributed event uncertainty, pending completion domains, and scalable pruning retain additional proof requirements.

evidence: Reviewed nonoverlap/overlap, pending operations, empty/full/close, exceptions, cancellations/timeouts/retries, duplicate values/IDs, mutable values, floating/unordered outcomes, and nondeterminism.
Reviewed missing/duplicate/reordered/dropped events, recorder overflow, logging serialization/unsafe probes, clock skew/uncertainty, crash durability, and redaction collision.

Reviewed factorial explosion, timeout/resource unknown, unsafe key/window decomposition, hash collisions, minimization causality, weak iteration, UAF/races, starvation, and adversarial checker denial-of-service.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage includes semantic, instrumentation, search, distributed-boundary, memory-safety, progress, and operational risks.

evidence: The checker constructs predecessor sets solely from response-before-invocation, selects only predecessor-ready operations, and applies an independent atomic-register state transition.
Recursive branches create new placed/remaining lists and scalar next state, preventing failed branches from contaminating siblings.
Exact assertions cover witness, invalid exhaustion, explored counts, valid and invalid real-time predecessor sets, and aggregate outcome.
invariant_checking.notes: The model assumes well-formed completed operations and trustworthy integer order; it intentionally lacks pending, malformed, timeout, memoization, and nondeterministic support.

evidence: Reviewed independent specification, API-boundary capture, partial-order construction, sequential search, pending completion, result normalization, and outcome taxonomy.
Reviewed memoization, locality/P-compositionality, window hazards, minimization/replay, adversarial generation, instrumentation effects, and artifact provenance.
Reviewed separation from memory safety and liveness, formal verification complement, alternatives, operational pipeline, and all exercise solutions.
proof_review.notes: Negative claims require completed sound search and faithful inputs; positive claims remain scoped to each observed interpreted history.

evidence: History-fidelity, decision, and evidence-scope arguments are separate proof structures with explicit assumptions.
Invalid is distinguished from unknown timeout/resource, malformed input, and unsupported specification.
Finite history checking, deterministic replay, generated stress, bounded model checking, memory tools, and mechanized/manual proof are separated by scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No final state, pass count, race-free run, checker timeout, witness, or minimized trace is generalized beyond what it establishes.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python checker passed exact ten-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It emits evidence=finite_history_search_model and reproduces one witness, one exhaustive finite counterexample, exact search counts, and real-time precedence.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed chapter validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No implementation threads, real recorder, pending calls, malformed histories, nondeterministic object, decomposition, timeout, weak-memory behavior, arbitrary schedule, model checking, progress, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives checking from histories and sequential state search, handles the formal and operational boundary cases, and presents testing as finite semantic evidence complementary to memory tools and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed independent oracles, event capture/noninterference, mutable normalization, pending/retry/cancellation, clock uncertainty, outcome taxonomy, pruning/decomposition, minimization/replay, generators, resource limits, CI artifacts, checker fixtures, and rollout use.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet gives the decision procedure and caveats; the executable checker contrasts overlapping-valid and ordered-invalid histories; ten examples cover frequent traps; five exercises provide complete tracing, audit, pipeline, and distributed transfer answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/maintainer-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Herlihy, Wing, Gong, Lowe, Horn, Kroening, Burckhardt, Dern, Musuvathi, Tan, Michael, Scott, Porcupine, OpenJDK, concurrency, distributed-systems, security, performance, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite checker prove neither a concrete concurrent implementation, recorder fidelity, pending/nondeterministic/distributed histories, scalable completeness under limits, decomposition/window soundness for a product spec, arbitrary schedules, weak-memory or memory safety, liveness, production checker performance, universal linearizability, certification, nor deployment fitness.
